summary: Michela Clemente is a Tibetologist who studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and completed postdoctoral training under Hildegard Diemberger (2013–2015). She held a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellowship at the University of Cambridge.
Michele Kerbaker (1835–1914) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He succeeded Giacomo Lignana in 1870 and held a post at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" from circa 1876 to 1914.

Michelle C. Wang works in art history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She completed her doctoral studies under Eugene Y. Wang (~2002–2008) and was appointed assistant professor of art and art history at Georgetown University around 2012.

Michelle Spuler (b. 1971) specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Queensland (~1995–2000) and taught at Victoria University of Wellington (~2001–2005) and Colorado College.

Michihiko Komine (b. 1945) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1963–1973), later serving there as assistant (~1973–1981) and professor (~1993–2016). He chaired the Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies (~2012–2016).

Michihiko Yajima (b. 1963) is an Indologist and linguist who was a graduate student at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981) and held a post there (attested 1992). He served as professor at Tsurumi University (attested 2003–2008).

Michihiro Ikeda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held lecturer posts at Setagaya Gakuen High School (attested 1996) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), and served as librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005).

Michiko Yusa (b. 1951) is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. She earned her PhD at UC Santa Barbara under Raimon Panikkar (~1976–1983) and served as professor of foreign languages at Western Washington University (~1983–2021).

Michio Kamikawa (b. 1960) specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ritsumeikan University (~1979–1988) and held an academic post at Aichi Prefectural University around 1998.

Michio Yano (b. 1944) is an Indologist and historian. He studied at Kyoto University (~1963–1972) and Brown University under David Pingree (~1978–1980), subsequently serving as a professor of cultural studies at Kyoto Sangyo University (~1974–2014).

Michitoshi Barada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Jien Abe, J. R. Joshi, and at Savitribai Phule Pune University (1997), later holding research posts at Otani University (attested 1992) and the Eastern Institute (attested 2000–2003).
Michiya Ito was a graduate student at Tohoku University (attested 1986–1990) and later held an academic post there (attested 2001–2004).

Michiyo Hoshi (b. 1941) specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. She has held researcher positions at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa and at Toyo Bunko (attested 2003).
Midori Nishino specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2006) and later worked there as a researcher (attested 2010–2015).

Migmar Tsering (1956–1999) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He taught Georges Dreyfus and John J. Makransky, served at CIHTS (attested 1990), and headed Sakya College (attested 1991–1997).

Mikaël Bauer works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kanazawa University under Paul Hoornaert and Noritoshi Aramaki, and completed his PhD at Harvard University under Ryuichi Abe (attested 2010).

Mikel Burley works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Essex, Bristol (PhD, 2005), under J. M. Bernstein, Jonardon Ganeri, Brian Carr, and John Peacock, becoming Associate Professor of Religion and Philosophy at Leeds (attested 2007–2020).
Mikio Otsuki specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held positions as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji and as a professor at Hanazono University (both attested 2007).

Mikisaburo Mori (1909–1986) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1929–1932) and held academic posts at Osaka University (~1950–1973) and Bukkyo University (~1973–1983).

Ming Mei specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Qingli Wan, and studied at SOAS under Roderick Whitfield, Tao Wang, Shane McCausland, and Andrey Terentyev.
